clue.text: President books the quarters within vast hotel compound

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

indicators.note: vast has four letters, so its two inner quarters are the letters left once each end is dropped

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A president hides books in the rooms of an enormous hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the quarters within' picks the middle two of the four letters of 'vast', giving AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium-based chemical substance, used chiefly in fertiliser, so it is a compound.

clue.text: Sites of culture hide priests after Reformation

indicators.note: a reformation reshapes something, so the letters of these two words are re-formed into a new order

explanation.surface: Priests going into hiding once the Reformation came, as Catholic priests in England did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sites of culture' looks like religious history, but a culture here is a lab growth of bacteria.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratory bacteria are grown as cultures in shallow glass plates of this kind, so they are where cultures sit.

clue.text: However tense, meditation can help with it

parts.note: though can mean however, as in 'it was late, though'
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: However stressed you feel, meditating may relieve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Meditation is deep reflection, and thought in the sense of contemplation is a synonym.

clue.text: Get a view of grasslands, say? Not from these

definitions.text: Get a view of grasslands, say? Not from these

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: get a view of means see, and grasslands are plains: see plains

explanation.surface: A question about where you would go to look out over prairies, answered with a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see plains' spoken sounds like the answer, and the joke is that aircraft that land on water are poor for seeing open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaplanes are aircraft that take off from and land on water, so you would sooner see the sea from one than prairie.

clue.text: American following Republican account — one doing spin about 50 states

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: spinning round turns these two pieces end to end

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A US political story: a Republican's account and a spin doctor working on the fifty states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing spin' turns AC plus I round to make ICA. 'about 50 states' looks like the USA, but this continent has 54 sovereign countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent is made up of roughly fifty-four sovereign countries, so 'about 50 states' describes it.

clue.text: Shrink from a man in uniform? On the contrary

indicators.note: in puts one piece within another; the following phrase says which way round
this flips the stated relation, so it is the uniform that goes inside the man rather than the man inside uniform

parts.note: Fred is a typical man's name
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone recoiling from a uniformed officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like a verb, but it is slang for a psychiatrist, the most famous being Sigmund Freud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud founded psychoanalysis, and a shrink is slang for a psychiatrist or analyst.

clue.text: Bake Off plugging trendy amateur technique for sorting out bloomers

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so the reworked letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of bake are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: The Great British Bake Off, a TV baking show, giving publicity to a fashionable amateur cooking method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like baked loaves after Bake Off, or underwear, but means flowers; 'Off' and 'plugging' are the anagram and insertion signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of arranging cut flowers, so it is a way of sorting out blooms.

clue.text: Drama for one held up by essentially extinct gag in Globe?

indicators.note: in a down entry, being held up by means sitting on top of what follows

parts.note: drama is one example of art

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter, of the word extinct

parts.note: to gag is to choke

explanation.surface: A play supported by an obsolete joke at the Globe, Shakespeare's theatre in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Globe' looks like the theatre, but the globe artichoke is a vegetable; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is the common edible thistle, so this word completes the name begun by Globe.

clue.text: Old Turk, German fellow and Middle Eastern state share a bank

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

indicators.note: a bank is an edge, so the two names overlap at the letter on their common edge and it is written only once

parts.note: Oman is a state on the Arabian Peninsula

explanation.surface: A Turk, a German and an Arab state using the same bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'share a bank' makes OTTO and OMAN overlap on one O. 'bank' looks financial but means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire was the old Turkish empire, and an Ottoman is a Turk of that era.

clue.text: Captivated by Cats — even the interval

indicators.note: being held captive by these words means the answer is held within them

explanation.surface: A theatregoer so enthralled by the musical Cats that even the interval is a pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interval' looks like the theatre break, but it is the musical gap between notes.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a seventh is the interval spanning seven notes of the scale, such as C up to B.

clue.text: Kinky heteros plus one?

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of heteros are bent into a new order

parts.note: the speaker, one, is me

explanation.surface: A straight couple with a bit of kink inviting someone else along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' rearranges HETEROS into THREESO, and 'one' read as the speaker gives ME. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight couple plus an extra person makes a group of three, especially in a sexual sense.

clue.text: "Hail Asgard!" stirred up legendary swordsman

indicators.note: stirring mixes something, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Norse warrior's battle cry to Asgard, the home of the gods in Norse myth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norse setting misleads: the answer comes from Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Galahad was the purest knight of King Arthur's Round Table, a sword-wielding hero of legend.

clue.text: Puckish entrance leading to bow

definitions.meaning: puckish means mischievous, like Puck; playfully knowing
...- as a prefix means chief or leading, as in archbishop
to ... is to curve or bow, as a cat ... its back

explanation.surface: A mischievous character making an entrance before taking a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is a dictionary meaning of the same short word: mischievous, curved doorway, chief, and to bend.

clue.text: Tube taken by someone who needs to rush off

definitions.text: Tube taken by someone who needs to rush off

parts.words: Tube taken by someone who needs to rush off
parts.note: reads like a London commuter catching the Underground, but the tube is a short hollow rod taken by a relay runner

explanation.surface: A hurried Londoner jumping on the Tube, the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like the London Underground; it is a hollow stick handed over in a relay race.
explanation.definitionFit: In relay races each runner takes this short hollow rod from a teammate and must sprint away with it.

clue.text: Bear who took in Mowgli takes another student around lair — it's got bigger

indicators.note: takes means takes in, so the extra letter goes inside the bear's name

parts.note: Baloo is the bear who looks after Mowgli in The Jungle Book
L, for learner, is a student; another because the bear's name already holds one

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for lair is written backwards

parts.note: a den is a lair

explanation.surface: Baloo from The Jungle Book adopting another pupil, and his den growing to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is there because the bear's name already holds one L; 'it's' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell rapidly, so ballooned means grew larger.

clue.text: Theatrical waiter could be on stage with a bit of rehearsal

indicators.note: could be means these letters might form something else, so they are rearranged
a bit of picks out only the first letter of the word rehearsal

explanation.surface: An actor playing a waiter going on stage after a little rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiter' looks like a restaurant job, but Estragon spends the whole play waiting for Godot.
explanation.definitionFit: Estragon is one of the two tramps who wait endlessly in Beckett's play Waiting for Godot.

clue.text: Girl initially put out by date refreshing Instagram to reveal trees

indicators.note: refreshing renews something, here remaking the letters into a new order
put out means ejected, so that letter is ousted and replaced by the next piece
initially picks the first letter of the word girl

explanation.surface: A girl rejected by a date who keeps refreshing Instagram, the photo app, for news.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping G for D in INSTAGRAM gives INSTARAM, which 'refreshing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamarinds are tropical leguminous trees grown for their sour pods.

clue.text: Is sleuth returning to open certain letters? …

definitions.note: the three dots are themselves the thing defined

indicators.note: to open means to break into, so the reversed pieces go inside

parts.note: an ell is the letter L, so ells are certain letters

indicators.note: returning means the words is and sleuth are read backwards

parts.note: PI, private investigator, is a sleuth

explanation.surface: A detective coming back to open some mail, the dots trailing off in suspense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' and 'to open' work on the pieces, and the definition is the trailing punctuation mark itself, which also leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dots marking an omission or a trailing-off are the punctuation mark of that name.

clue.text: Experts in viewing presumably discussed cool episodes

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken, so the phrase is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: eye sages, wise ones of the eye, would presumably be experts in viewing

explanation.surface: Television critics talking about chilled-out episodes of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool episodes' sounds like TV, but means freezing periods in Earth's history.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacial periods are long cold phases of geological history, so they are chilly episodes.

clue.text: … maybe second set of lines found after second reading?

definitions.note: three dots are an example of this signalling system, standing for the letter S

indicators.note: found after means the earlier pieces come after the later ones in the answer

parts.note: a mo, a moment, is a second
R, for reading, is one of the three Rs
an ode is a poem, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A second batch of poetry discovered after rereading, trailing on from the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening dots continue the last clue but are also the definition: dot-dot-dot is S in this telegraph code.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dots are the letter S in the telegraph signalling system of dots and dashes.

clue.text: Unable to sit still, Methuselah has to follow others

indicators.note: to follow means the setter's piece comes after the other one

parts.note: the rest means the others
Methuselah is the setter, so Methuselah has is I've

explanation.surface: An old man fidgeting, made to trail behind everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is the setter's pseudonym, so the name stands for I, and has makes I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive means fidgety or restless, unable to keep still.

clue.text: See 18
Pressure mounting on firm given millions for making stuff up

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the pressure pieces follow the firm pieces

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
mounting means rising

explanation.surface: A company under growing pressure, handed millions for inventing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making stuff up' looks like lying but means constituting.
explanation.definitionFit: To comprise is to constitute or make up a whole, so the -ing form means making something up.

clue.text: Stop account deletion, tapping escape key with only seconds left

indicators.note: only seconds left means all but the second letter of each word is thrown away

explanation.surface: A computer user trying to halt an account deletion by pressing the Escape key, with seconds to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like time running out, but it means the second letters of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to come to a halt, so it is a synonym of stop.

clue.text: Band's new sound has tenor going low

definitions.note: Band's is band is; the answer is a band of nine

indicators.note: in a down entry going low means sinking to the bottom, so that letter moves to the end

parts.note: a tone is a sound

explanation.surface: A group's fresh sound has its tenor singing in a lower register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going low' moves the T of TONE to the end, giving ONET.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, so it is a kind of band.

clue.text: Italian visiting England masters puzzles

indicators.note: visiting means staying inside, so the Italian goes into England

parts.note: MAs are Masters of Arts

explanation.surface: An Italian visitor to England baffling some masters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmas are mysteries or riddles, synonyms for puzzles as nouns.

clue.text: State has some humanitarian aid nicked in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution means turned round, so the picked letters are read backwards
some means only part of these words is taken

explanation.surface: Revolutionaries stealing some of the aid sent to a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ANAIDNI from the middle of the words, and 'in revolution' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: See 1
Agree to attempt short back and sides for narcissist

indicators.note: back means the shortened word is turned round
short means cut off at the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: an essay is an attempt

indicators.note: sides means the outer letters of the word narcissist

explanation.surface: Consenting to give a vain man a short back and sides, a British barber's standard short haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: The haircut phrase is a decoy split across three jobs: 'short' trims, 'back' turns round, and 'sides' takes the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to give one's consent, so it is a synonym of agree.
